claims.behaviour: `issue-constant-icon-cache` keeps the HTML it rendered in memory, keyed per input (see the key claim), with no size limit. The whole cache is emptied (not entry by entry) on first use and on the first lookup made more than the time-to-live after the last emptying; the time-to-live is read once at construction from the dark feature `structure.iconConstantCache.ttl` in seconds, default 300 (5 minutes); the same property governs all three icon caches. Within that window a repeated lookup for the same key returns the stored HTML without asking Jira again, even if the underlying icon, name or avatar changed.

`issue-constant-icon-cache` is a `CachingComponent`: `clearCaches()`, `clearUserCaches(user)` and `clearUserCaches(userKey)` each empty the whole cache (not just one user's entries) and restart the time-to-live window, so the next lookup renders anew.

For a Jira `IssueConstant` (issue type, priority, status, resolution) `issue-constant-icon-cache` returns ``, where NAME is the constant's name translated with the `AttributeContext`'s i18n helper (`getNameTranslation`) and URL the absolute icon URL (see the URL claim); both are HTML-escaped with Jira's `TextUtils.htmlEncode`.

The icon URL is the constant's `getIconUrl()` trimmed: when it starts with `http://` or `https://` it is used as is, otherwise it is prefixed with Jira's base URL from SAL `ApplicationProperties.getBaseUrl()` (trimmed; empty when the SAL service is missing), with no slash added between them.
`issue-constant-icon-cache` returns the empty string (and caches it) for a null constant, and for a constant whose icon URL is null, blank or exactly `/`.

Entries of `issue-constant-icon-cache` are keyed by the constant's Java class simple name, its id and the `AttributeContext`'s locale (`<SimpleName>:<id>:<locale>`), so the same constant is rendered separately per locale, and an issue type and a priority with the same id do not collide. A null constant has key `""`. The base URL is not part of the key.

For a user, `user-icon-cache` asks SAL `UserManager.getUserProfile(username)` and takes `getProfilePictureUri(w, h)` with w = h = the pixel size of Jira's small avatar (`Avatar.Size.SMALL`, 24 on Jira 9). It returns ``, where NAME is the HTML-escaped `ApplicationUser.getName()` and AVATAR the profile picture URI as given (not escaped). HTML escaping uses Jira's `TextUtils.htmlEncode`.

For a null user, or a user for whom SAL returns no profile, `user-icon-cache` returns ``, where BASE is the `AttributeContext`'s base URL and ID Jira's anonymous avatar id from `AvatarManager.getAnonymousAvatarId()` (looked up once per `AttributeContext` and kept in it).
Entries of `user-icon-cache` are keyed by the user's key only (not by locale or base URL); a null user has key `""`. A user without a profile is cached under its own key with the anonymous HTML.

For a user, `user-printable-icon-cache` asks SAL `UserManager.getUserProfile(username)` and takes `getProfilePictureUri(w, h)` with w = h = the pixel size of Jira's small avatar (`Avatar.Size.SMALL`, 24 on Jira 9). It returns ``, where USERNAME is the HTML-escaped `getUsername()`, DISPLAY the HTML-escaped `getDisplayName()` and AVATAR the profile picture URI as given (not escaped). HTML escaping uses Jira's `TextUtils.htmlEncode`.

For a null user, or a user for whom SAL returns no profile, `user-printable-icon-cache` returns ``, where BASE is the `AttributeContext`'s base URL and ID Jira's anonymous avatar id from `AvatarManager.getAnonymousAvatarId()` (looked up once per `AttributeContext` and kept in it).

Entries of `user-printable-icon-cache` are keyed by the user's key only (not by locale or base URL); a null user has key `""`. A user without a profile is cached under its own key with the anonymous HTML.
`user-field-renderer` returns null for a null user and for a user for whom SAL `UserManager.getUserProfile(username)` returns no profile.

For a user with a SAL profile, `user-field-renderer` renders the Velocity template `/templates/structure/field/user.vm` (its own resource) with Jira's `VelocityTemplatingEngine` as HTML (`asHtml()`), with Jira's default Velocity parameters for the current user (from `VelocityRequestContextFactory.getDefaultVelocityParams` and the plugin's authentication context) plus: `url` = Jira base URL + the profile's `getProfilePageUri()`, `username` = profile user name, `displayName` = profile full name, `avatarUrl` = the profile's `getProfilePictureUri()` (default size), `view` = the requested view mode or `""` when null. The extra parameters win over the defaults.

The rendered HTML depends on the view mode. `avatar`: a link `` holding only the extra-small avatar (``). `name`: the same link holding only the display name as text. Any other value (including none): the same link holding the avatar followed by `DISPLAYNAME`. Whether values are HTML-escaped depends on Jira's Velocity escaping at run time.

`item-property-editors` gives an editor for the item property name `notes` (the built-in default note; never archived) and for `dc_note_<n>` when `note-manager` knows a note with that id (archived or not, remembering whether it is archived at lookup time). For any other name, or a `dc_note_` name with no stored note, it gives no editor (null), so the property cannot be edited through the item update REST call.

Editing through an editor stores the value as the item property (structure id, item, property name = the note id `notes` / `dc_note_<n>`) via the plugin's per-structure item property store (`AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_PROPERTY`; a blank value deletes the row there). Errors are not thrown: they are added as error messages to the given Jira `ErrorCollection` and nothing is stored.

An edit is refused, with exactly one error message and nothing stored, in this order: the note is archived (text of `s.itemproperty.notes.edit.archived.unavailable`, English `Cannot edit or add values for archived notes.`); the item does not resolve through `ItemResolver.resolveItem(item, Object.class)` (`s.itemproperty.notes.edit.unavailable` with the item description, `Cannot edit notes for an unavailable item: {0}.`); the `ForestSpec` has no structure id or id 0 (`s.itemproperty.notes.edit.no.structure`, `Notes can be edited only for a particular structure.`); the current user lacks EDIT on the structure per `StructureManager.isAccessible(id, EDIT)` (`s.item.edit.error.no-edit-perm` with the structure id, `No "Edit" permission for structure {0}.`). The note's own permission scheme is not consulted.

When the item property store rejects the write with `IllegalArgumentException` (for example a property key it cannot encode) or fails with a storage error, the editor adds the error message `s.itemproperty.notes.edit.failed` (`Failed to update notes.`) and returns normally.

`note-searcher` searches the built-in default note (id `notes`, name = text of `s.w.notes.note.default`, English `Notes (Default)`) and every non-archived stored note. A note matches when the term is the empty string, or when the term, trimmed, occurs anywhere in the note's name as literal text (no wildcards or regex), ignoring case (Unicode-aware).

A term made only of whitespace matches no note at all (the empty-term rule applies only to the untrimmed empty string), so the result has no groups and no more-results flag (as the original does). A null term throws `NullPointerException`.

Results come as groups in this order, each present only when non-empty: (1) an untitled group with just the default note, if it matches; (2) the group titled `s.w.notes.note.search.used-notes` (`Used in structure`): matching stored notes that have at least one value in the given structure, only when the current user can VIEW that structure (`StructureManager.isAccessible`); (3) the group titled `s.w.notes.note.search.other-notes` (`Other notes`), computed only while the limit is not exceeded: matching notes not yet listed that have a value in any structure the current user can VIEW, plus the remaining matching notes whose permission scheme gives the current user view access (per `permission-scheme-manager`). Each note appears in at most one group.

Notes listed because they have values in the given structure or in another structure the user can view are listed regardless of the note's own permission scheme; only notes with no values in a viewable structure need the scheme's view permission.
Within groups 2 and 3, notes are sorted by name with plain case-sensitive `String` order, then by id as a string (so `dc_note_10` comes before `dc_note_9`).

With a null limit every group is complete and the more-results flag is false. With limit L, groups are taken in order while the remaining count is positive; a group is cut to the remaining count, and after each group the remaining count drops by the group's full size. A group met when the remaining count is 0 is left out. The more-results flag (REST `hasMore`) is true when the remaining count went below 0, i.e. more matching notes were found than L. Example: L = 2 with the default note and 3 used notes gives the default note, the first used note, and `hasMore` true; group 3 is not computed.
Limit 0 gives no groups; `hasMore` is true when at least one note matches, false when none does. A negative limit gives no groups and `hasMore` true, even when no note matches at all.

`saved-column-manager` knows exactly two saved-column sources, listed in this order: `bundled` (`bundled-column-source`) then `stored` (`stored-column-source`). Looking a source up by id gives that source for `bundled` or `stored`, and nothing (null) for any other id; REST calls on another source id fail as not found.

A view column refers to a saved column through its parameter `savedColumn`, whose text must be `[modified/]<sourceId>/<columnId>` with a decimal column id; the source id is everything between the optional `modified/` prefix and the last `/`. A value of another shape makes adjusting the view specification throw `IllegalArgumentException` (`Column id does not match the declared format: ...`). Columns without the parameter are left untouched, as are columns whose source id is unknown.

When a view specification is adjusted for a user, each column with an unmodified reference `<source>/<id>` is looked up in its source ignoring permissions: if the saved column no longer exists the column is removed from the specification; otherwise the column's key becomes the saved column's type and its parameters are replaced by the saved column's parameters, plus `savedColumn` = `<source>/<id>` when the user may read the saved column, without it when not. The column's csid and name are kept; column order and other columns are unchanged.

A column with a `modified/<source>/<id>` reference keeps its own key and parameters. If the user may not read that saved column (including when it no longer exists), the `savedColumn` parameter is removed from the column; otherwise the column is left as it is.

Every `StructureView` returned by `view-manager` reports its specification adjusted this way, with the security override and user key that were current when the view object was obtained; the stored view data in `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW` is not changed by it.

`stored-column-source` has source id `stored` and two lists in this order: `global` (name = text of `s.w.saved-column.list.global`, English `Global`) with every global saved column (`AO_8BAD1B_SAVED_COLUMN` rows with `C_OWNER` NULL), and `user` (`s.w.saved-column.list.user`, `My Columns`) with the current user's own columns. Anonymous users get an empty `user` list; with security overridden the `user` list holds every user's columns (read uncached). Each saved column's list key is `global` without owner and `user` with one.

The `global` list reports create-supported when security is overridden or `StructurePluginHelper.isManageGlobalSavedColumnsAllowed(current user)` is true; the `user` list when the user is not anonymous (or security is overridden).

Listing, reading, creating, updating, moving and deleting stored columns first require, unless security is overridden, that `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToUser(current user)` is true (the user found by key; null for anonymous); otherwise they throw `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED`. The readable/editable/movable checks do not make this check.
Reading one stored column by id returns it when it exists and is global, or is owned by the current user, or security is overridden; another user's column and a missing id give null (not an error).

Creating into list `user` stores a personal column owned by the current user (anonymous: `StructureException` `SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED`, even with security overridden but no user); into `global` stores a column with no owner and requires security override or the manage-global-saved-columns permission (`SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED` otherwise); any other list key throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`List is not supported: <key>`). Type and parameters are not validated here; the name is mandatory, and a blank one or one over 190 characters is refused when the input is read. The new row goes into `AO_8BAD1B_SAVED_COLUMN` (via `saved-column-io`).

Updating or deleting a stored column: a missing id throws `StructureException` `SAVED_COLUMN_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. Unless security is overridden: a global column requires the manage-global-saved-columns permission (`SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED`); a personal column requires a logged-in user (`SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED` for anonymous) who is its owner (`SAVED_COLUMN_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for another user's column). Nothing is changed when a check fails.

A stored column can be moved only to list `global`: the move is allowed when the column exists, has an owner, the owner is the current user (or security is overridden) and the user may manage global saved columns (or security is overridden). The move clears `C_OWNER`, making the column global. A refused move throws `StructureException` `SAVED_COLUMN_MANAGEMENT_DENIED`; there is no way back to `user`.

When asked whether a move is possible with an error collection, a refused move adds one general error: target list not `global`, or column owned by someone else, or no manage-global permission: `s.w.saved-column.error.user-cannot-move` with the target list key (`User cannot move column to {0}`); missing column: `s.w.saved-column.error.not-found.edit` (`Unable to edit the saved column because it has been deleted`); column already global: `s.w.saved-column.error.column-moved-to-global` (`Cannot edit saved column because it has been moved to global`).

A stored column is readable when it exists and (security overridden, or it is global, or the current user owns it). It is editable when it exists and (security overridden, or the current user owns it, or it is global and the user may manage global saved columns). Missing columns are neither. This editable answer is what REST reports as `editable`.

For backup, the extra data of a stored column is `{"owner": <user key>}` for a personal column and null for a global or missing one. Restoring from backup: creating from backup stores a personal column for the given `owner` (any value turned to text) or a global column when there is no owner; restoring with an explicit id recreates the row with that id and owner. All three need security overridden, otherwise `StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` (`This operation is only available in sudo context`).

The replacement does no licence checking: creating, updating, moving and deleting stored saved columns are never refused or made read-only on licence grounds (SPEC.md §1.1, §1.8), although the REST descriptions mention a licence read-only mode.

`bundled-column-source` has source id `bundled` and one list with key `bundled`, named by the text of `s.w.saved-column.list.bundled` (English `Bundled`), never create-supported. Every bundled column is readable by anyone (no permission check, also for anonymous users), never editable or movable, and its list key is `bundled`. Creating, updating, moving or deleting a bundled column throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Reading by an unknown id gives null.

Every bundled column has type `formula`; its name and description are i18n texts looked up with the plugin helper's i18n (current user's locale) each time they are read. Its parameters hold `formula` (the expression text), usually `variables` (a map from variable name to an attribute spec `{"id": <attribute id>, "format": <value format id>}`, plus `params` where noted) and usually `displayFormat`. Unless stated, a bundled column is neither featured nor should-open-configurator.

The bundled columns are built on first use and then kept for the life of the component. Which of them exist and how they look (see the story points and sprint claims) is decided once, from the fields visible to the user who triggered that first use.

The bundled list holds, in this order: 1 BugFix % (Time), 2 BugFix % (Count), WSJF (Basic) as 3 (story points field found) or 4 (not found), 5 WSJF (Tempo), 6 WSJF (SAFe), 7 Total Work Ratio (Points) (only with a story points field), 8 Total Work Ratio (Time), 9 Total Underestimation, 10 Time to Resolve, 11 Due In, 12 Time Since Last Update, 13 Assignee Cost, 14 Unresolved Blockers, 15 Item Health, 16 Tasks Since Sprint Started (only when a Sprint field exists), 17 Time Flagged. The numbers are the column ids (REST `bundled/<id>`).

The story points field is the first field, in the order Jira's `FieldManager.getAvailableNavigableFields(current user)` returns them, whose name, lower-cased with `Locale.US` and stripped of every character that is not a letter or digit, equals `storypoints` (so `Story Points`, `Story-points`, `story_points` all match). Its variable spec is the field turned into an attribute spec with format `number`: a custom field `customfield_<n>` gives `{"id": "customfield", "format": "number", "params": {"fieldId": <n>}}`, a system field `{"id": <field id>, "format": "number"}`.

The Sprint field is the custom field that `gh-integration` reports as Jira Software's Sprint field; none when it reports none. Its variable spec is `{"id": "customfield", "format": "text", "params": {"fieldId": <n>}}`.

Bundled column 1, name key `s.w.formula.preset.bugfixPercent.time` (English `BugFix % (Time)`, description key with `.description`: `Displays percent of time spent on fixing bugs`), is featured. Variables: `type` = `issuetype` (text), `timespent` = `timespent` (duration), `estimate` = `timeestimate` (duration). Formula: total = sum over the sub-tree (including the row) of time spent + remaining estimate; when total > 0, the same sum over rows whose type is `bug`, divided by total (no value otherwise). Display format `{"type": "percentage", "rounding": 0}`.

Bundled column 2, `s.w.formula.preset.bugfixPercent.count` (`BugFix % (Count)`, `Displays percent of all sub-issues that are bugs`). Variables: `type` = `issuetype` (text), `itemtype` = `itemtype` (text). Formula: total = sum over the sub-tree of 1 for each row whose item type is `issue`; when total > 0, the count of rows of type `bug` divided by total, else 0. Display format percentage, rounding 0.

WSJF (Basic), `s.w.formula.preset.wsjf` (`WSJF (Basic)`, `Weighted Shortest Job First, a measurement of issues benefit/cost ratio`), is featured; id 3 when a story points field exists, else id 4. Variables: `priority` = `priority` (text), `votes` = `votes` (number), `duedate` = `duedate` (time), `remainingestimate` = `timeestimate` (duration), `resolution` = `resolution` (text), `itemtype` = `itemtype` (text), `watches` = `watches` (number), and for id 3 also `storypoints` = the story points spec. Formula, only for unresolved rows of item type `issue`: priority value (Highest 160, High 80, Medium 40, Low 20, Lowest 10, otherwise 40) × interest (1 + votes + watches / 10) × due factor (1.5 with a due date, else 1) × 100, divided by 1 + cost. Id 3 cost: (10 + calendar hours of the remaining estimate / 4 when set) + (10 + story points / 4 when set) + (20 when neither is set). Id 4 cost: 10 + calendar hours of the remaining estimate / 4 when set, else 20. Display format `{"type": "number", "rounding": 0}`.

Bundled column 5, `s.w.formula.preset.wsjf.alm` (`WSJF (Tempo)`, `Weighted Shortest Job First metric, according to categories suggested by Tempo`), should open the configurator. Only variable: `itemtype` = `itemtype` (text); the others (`Benefit`, `Pain`, `Marketability`, `Impact`, `Cost`, `Risk`, `Clarity`) are left for the user to bind. Formula, for rows of item type `issue`: 100 × Bang / Buck, where Bang = (1 + benefit + pain + marketing) × impact and Buck = 1 + cost × risk × clarity, with the mappings benefit Low 1 / Medium 2 / High 5 / else 0; pain Low 1 / Medium 3 / High 6 / else 0; marketing (Marketability) Medium 1 / High 4 / else 0; impact Low 0.8 / Medium 1.2 / High 2 / else 1; cost Low 1 / Medium 1.5 / High 3 / else 2; risk Low 1 / Medium 1.5 / High 3 / else 2; clarity Medium 1 / High 0.9 / else 1.5. Display format number, rounding 0.

Bundled column 6, `s.w.formula.preset.wsjf.safe` (`WSJF (SAFe)`, `Weighted Shortest Job First metric, as suggested by Scaled Agile, Inc`), should open the configurator and has no `variables` parameter. Its formula is a template with placeholders `Size_Field_Or_Expression`, `Value_Field_Or_Expression`, `Criticality_Field_Or_Expression`, `RiskReduction_Field_Or_Expression`, `Opportunity_Field_Or_Expression` for job size, user-business value, time criticality, risk reduction and opportunity enablement; cost of delay = value + criticality + (risk reduction or, if that is empty, opportunity enablement); result, when job size > 0: cost of delay / job size. Display format `{"type": "number", "rounding": 2}`.

Bundled column 7 (only with a story points field), `s.w.formula.preset.wr.points` (`Total Work Ratio (Points)`). Variables: `storypoints` = the story points spec, `resolution` = `resolution` (text). Formula: when the sum of story points over the sub-tree is > 0, the sum of story points of resolved rows divided by it. Display format `{"type": "percentage", "rounding": 1}`.

Bundled column 8, `s.w.formula.preset.wr.time` (`Total Work Ratio (Time)`). Variables: `timespent` = `timespent` (duration), `estimate` = `timeestimate` (duration). Formula: spent = sum of time spent over the sub-tree, remaining = sum of remaining estimate; when spent + remaining > 0, spent / (spent + remaining). Display format percentage, rounding 1.

Bundled column 9, `s.w.formula.preset.time.underestimation` (`Total Underestimation`). Variables: `timespent` = `timespent`, `remaining` = `timeestimate`, `original_estimate` = `timeoriginalestimate` (all duration). Formula: original = sum of original estimates over the sub-tree; when original > 0, (sum of time spent + remaining over the sub-tree − original) / original. Display format percentage, rounding 1.

Bundled columns 10–12 all use display format `{"type": "duration", "workTime": false}`. 10 `s.w.formula.preset.time.ttr` (`Time to Resolve`): variables `resolved` = `resolutiondate` (time), `created` = `created` (time); when resolved is set, resolved − created. 11 `s.w.formula.preset.time.duein` (`Due In`): variable `duedate` = `duedate` (time); when the due date is set, due date − now if positive, otherwise the text `Overdue`. 12 `s.w.formula.preset.time.tslu` (`Time Since Last Update`): variable `updated` = `updated` (time); when set, now − updated.

Bundled column 13, `s.w.formula.preset.time.cost-assignee` (`Σ Assignee Cost`). Variables: `assignee` = `assignee` (text), `remainingestimate` = `timeestimate` (duration), `timespent` = `timespent` (duration), `rate` = attribute `user-property` (text) with params `{"userKey": {"id": "assignee", "format": "text"}, "propertyName": "Hourly Rate"}`. Formula: when the row has an assignee and a rate and remaining + spent > 0, rate × calendar hours of (remaining + spent). Other parameters: `aggregate` = `sum`, `distinct` = true, `forestSpec` = `displayed`; no display format.

Bundled column 14, `s.w.formula.preset.unresolved-blockers` (`Unresolved Blockers`). Variables: `issuelinks` = `issuelinkobjects` (any), `this` = `item` (any). Formula: from the row's issue links, those of link type `blocks` whose destination is this item and whose source is unresolved, giving their source issues (an array). No display format.

Bundled column 15, `s.w.formula.preset.item-health` (`Item Health`). Variable `progress` = attribute `progress` (number) with params `{"basedOn": "timetracking", "includeSelf": true, "resolvedComplete": true}`. Formula: a wiki-markup panel showing a status by progress: > 0.7 `Great` (background `59B161`, Structure icon `shine`, padding 12); > 0.3 `OK` (`FFAF00`, `partly-cloudy`, 21); otherwise `At Risk` (`EF4B59`, `thunderbolt`, 7). Each panel is borderless with that background colour, the 20×20 icon, a spacer image of the padding width, the status in bold white, and another spacer (icons by URL from the Structure icon set, including `spacer`). Display format `{"type": "wiki"}`.

Bundled column 16 (only when a Sprint field exists), `s.w.formula.preset.tasks-since-sprint` (`Tasks Since Sprint Started`). Variables: `history` = `history` (any), `sprint` = the Sprint field spec. Formula: over the sub-tree, counts rows whose latest change of field `sprint` happened after the start date of the latest of the row's sprints. Display format number, rounding 0.

Bundled column 17, `s.w.formula.preset.time-flagged` (`Time Flagged`). Variable `history` = `history` (any). Formula: from the change history of field `flagged`, takes the times it was set to `Impediment` and the times it was cleared (set to empty); when it was flagged at least once, the sum over each flag-on time of (the matching clear time by position, or now when there is none) minus the flag-on time. Display format duration, workTime false.

`extension-service` keeps, for each extension module type, the modules of that type that are enabled in Jira (from any plugin, via `PluginAccessor.getEnabledModuleDescriptorsByClass`): `structure-item-type` (item types), the generator types `structure-inserter`, `structure-extender`, `structure-grouper`, `structure-filter`, `structure-sorter` (one generator catalogue), `structure-synchronizer`, `structure-effector`, `structure-effect-provider`, `structure-attribute-loader-provider`, `structure-export-renderer-provider`, `structure-query-constraint`, `structure-core-extension`, `structure-performance-log-provider`, `structure-query-skeleton-factory`, `structure-backup-provider`, `structure-calendar-provider` and `structure-integration-details-provider`. With no enabled module of a type the corresponding catalogue is empty.

Each catalogue is built on first request and reused until a module of that type is enabled or disabled (Atlassian `PluginModuleEnabledEvent` / `PluginModuleDisabledEvent`, listened to while started); then it is rebuilt on the next request. Each such change also asks for all plugin caches to be cleared, throttled to at most once per `structure.clear.cache.min.interval` ms (dark feature, default 1000): every enabled `CachingComponent` module gets `clearCaches()`.

On start the component registers for plugin events, drops all catalogues and clears all plugin caches at once (every enabled `CachingComponent`). Before start, requests are served (built from Jira but not refreshed by events). After stop it unregisters, drops all catalogues, ignores module events and answers every request with the empty catalogue; it cannot be started again after a stop.

A module whose `getModule()` throws (any `Exception` or `LinkageError`) or returns an object of the wrong type is left out of its catalogue with a warning; it does not fail the catalogue or the caller.

Attribute loader providers, synchronizers and query constraints (module types with an order) are taken in ascending order using Jira's module descriptor comparator; other types are taken in the order Jira returns them. Attribute loader providers and synchronizers read the order from the `order` attribute (default 0); query constraints read it from an `<order>` child element (default `Integer.MAX_VALUE`).

Item types, generators, synchronizers, effectors and effect providers are looked up by the module's complete key (`<plugin key>:<module key>`, for example `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`); an unknown key gives null (the item type for a null `ItemIdentity` is null). Core extensions, query skeleton factories and calendar providers are maps by complete key; when two modules share a key, the later one wins with a warning. Attribute loader providers and performance log providers are plain lists.

Resolving a generator by complete key throws `StructureException` `UNAVAILABLE_MODULE` (`Generator module <key> is not found`) when no enabled generator module has that key, and `UNAVAILABLE_MODULE` (`Generator module <key> failed to resolve`) when its module object cannot be obtained as a `StructureGenerator`; otherwise it gives the generator bound to the given parameters and owning structure. The generator catalogue also tells whether a key is present and lists all generator modules.

The effector catalogue keeps every enabled `structure-effector` module by complete key (even one whose module object fails to load) and gives its count; the `Effector` object for a key is obtained on each request, null when missing or failing.

Export renderer providers are indexed by (column key, export format). A module without column keys is filed under the null column key, one without formats under the null format. A format name that `ExportFormat.forExternalName` does not know is skipped with a warning. A lookup returns exactly the providers filed under the given (column key, format) pair, in module order, or an empty list; providers filed under null keys are not merged into lookups for specific keys.

Query constraints are indexed by the module's `fname` attribute. A name that is empty, contains anything but Latin letters, digits and underscore, or is an S-JQL keyword is rejected with a warning. When several modules have the same name, the one with the lowest order (its `<order>` child element, default `Integer.MAX_VALUE`) wins (on equal order the first one met stays), with a warning naming both.

Every newly built item type catalogue and query constraint catalogue gets a version number from one counter shared by both kinds, starting at 0 when the plugin loads and growing by 1 per catalogue built (empty placeholder catalogues included), so callers can tell that the catalogue changed.

Backup providers are kept by the providing plugin's key (one per plugin; with several, the last one met wins). Integration details providers are kept by module key (not complete key), each reported together with its plugin's name; two such modules with the same module key in different plugins make building that catalogue throw `IllegalStateException` (as the original does).

`ao-based-view-manager` is the store and logic behind `view-manager`: everything claimed for `view-manager` (views in `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW`, per-structure and default settings in `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW`, associations in `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE`, permissions, menus) is carried out here; `view-manager` adds only the one-time creation of the default views before first use.

Loaded views, per-structure view settings and per-view lists of associated structures are each cached in memory and dropped one hour after their last access (dark feature `structure.view.cache.timeout` in seconds, default 3600; the JVM system property `structure.cache.expiration-override` overrides it). The list of all view ids is cached without expiry. Saving a view drops that view's entry; creating a view drops the id list; deleting a view drops its entry, its associated-structure list and the id list; writing a structure's settings drops that structure's settings entry and every associated-structure list.

As a `CachingComponent`, `clearCaches()` drops all four caches (views, all view ids, structure settings, view-to-structures), so the next calls re-read Active Objects; `clearUserCaches(user)` does nothing.

Saving a new view requires, unless security is overridden, that `StructurePluginHelper.isViewCreationAllowed(current user)` is true; otherwise `StructureException` `VIEW_CREATION_DENIED` and nothing is stored.

Unless security is overridden, saving a view whose permission rules are non-empty (a new view, or an existing view whose rules change) requires `StructurePluginHelper.isViewSharingAllowed(current user)`: otherwise `StructureException` `VIEW_CREATION_DENIED` for a new view, `VIEW_EDIT_DENIED` for an existing one. An empty rule list never needs the sharing right.

The view's rules are then validated in list order, first failure wins, with the same rules as for structures (see `structure-manager`'s rule validation): a `SetLevel` with a null subject gives `INVALID_PARAMETER`; a user subject needs the current user to hold Jira's `USER_PICKER` permission and the key to resolve (error code 6013 otherwise); a group must be among the current user's available groups (6010); a project role needs a non-zero project (`INVALID_PARAMETER`), a project among the current user's structure projects (6011) and an existing role (6012). An apply-structure rule is never allowed in a view's rules: error code 6007 (`APPLY_RULE_NOT_APPLICABLE`). Errors carry the view id.

When saving changes to an existing view, the pending changes are first applied to the view as loaded (blank name: `INVALID_PARAMETER`), then applied again to the row's current `C_DATA`; if that result is invalid (for example the stored JSON has no specification) the save fails with `StructureException` `GENERIC_ERROR` for the view and the row is not changed.

Restoring a view (backup restore) requires a complete view with a non-zero id, a non-blank name and a specification (`StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` otherwise) and inserts the `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW` row with that id and the view's JSON as `C_DATA`, without permission, owner or sharing checks. It does not refresh the cached list of all view ids.

For backup the manager can list every `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW` row as structure id (0 = global default) → raw `C_VIEW_SETTINGS` text (possibly null), sorted by structure id, without access checks.
Looking a view up by id without access checks gives the stored view, or nothing when it is missing, unreadable or the id is not positive (the failure is logged, not thrown).
A view's owner is reported as the Jira user with the stored owner's user key, or null when there is no owner, the owner is not a user subject, or no Jira user has that key.

A view counts as shared when its rule list contains an apply-structure rule or a set-level rule with a level other than NONE, met before the end of the list. It counts as public when, walking the rules in order, the last decisive rule is "anyone gets VIEW or more": such a rule makes it public, while a rule setting NONE (for any subject) or an apply-structure rule makes it not public; other set-level rules leave the answer unchanged; no rules: not public.

Making a view public replaces its pending rules with: anyone VIEW first, then copies of the existing set-level rules whose level is above VIEW (EDIT, ADMIN) in their order; VIEW and NONE rules and apply-structure rules are dropped. Nothing is stored until the view is saved.

At start the manager registers a statistics source with `statistics-manager` reporting `averagePinnedColumnsCount`, `maximumPinnedColumnsCount` and `viewsWithPinCount` (as doubles) over the views that have at least one pinned column. Only views currently held in the view cache are counted (views not loaded since the cache was last cleared or expired are ignored) (as the original does). With no such view the source reports nothing (empty map); views that fail to load are skipped.
The replacement does no licence checking: saving, deleting views and writing view settings never fail on licence grounds (see `view-manager`).
